summary: Checked the Python 3.15 Windows build. check-wheels.py 3.15 exits 0 and reports 'OK - 33 wheels', which include pymongo-4.19.0-cp315-cp315-win_amd64, pydantic_core-2.50.1-cp315-cp315-win_amd64, bcrypt-5.0.0-cp39-abi3-win_amd64, greenlet-3.5.6-cp315-cp315-win_amd64, watchfiles-1.3.0-cp310-abi3-win_amd64, playwright-1.57.0-py3-none-win_amd64, motor-3.7.1, pydantic-2.14.1 and fastapi-0.110.1. The 3.12 and 3.13 runs also print 'OK - 33 wheels'. Their exit code showed as 1 only because my '| head' broke the pipe; that was not a script fault. Dependency metadata has no conflicts: motor requires pymongo>=4.9,<5 (4.19.0 installed), pydantic 2.14.1 requires pydantic-core==2.50.1, and fastapi requires pydantic<3 and starlette>=0.37.2,<0.38. In a fresh Python 3.11 venv, 'pip install -r requirements-windows.txt' resolved to the same versions and 'pip check' found nothing broken. Uvicorn on port 8003 returned: health 200; admin login 200 with httpOnly access_token and refresh_token cookies; 200 for items?lite=1, crm/quotations, purchase-orders and work-orders; 422 for POST /api/items with missing fields (pydantic 2.14 error format). The server log had no errors. The server was stopped and the venv deleted. Static checks: setup.bat is CRLF on all 127 lines, and the 3.15 and 3.14 echo lines are single-line 'if' statements outside any block with no parentheses. check-wheels.py compiles and imports only stdlib modules (subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil, os).
critical_code_review_comments: Optional: check-wheels.py raises BrokenPipeError when its output is piped to head. This is cosmetic. Requirements use open-ended ranges, such as watchfiles>=1.1.1 and pydantic_core>=2.41.5 without an upper bound, so future releases could change the resolved set. Pydantic pins pydantic-core exactly, which limits this risk.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Verified with pymongo 4.19.0, pydantic 2.14.1 / core 2.50.1, bcrypt 5.0.0, motor 3.7.1. Previous iteration_160 verified pymongo 4.18.3.
